title: Frankfort: Frank's Ford becomes the capital
summary: Frankfort began as a buffalo-trail ford on the Kentucky River, named for pioneer Stephen Frank, who was killed in a skirmish there in 1780.
bodyMarkdown:
Before Frankfort was a town, the site was a ford across the Kentucky River on one of the great buffalo trails. English explorers first visited the [Frankfort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankfort,_Kentucky) area in the 1750s. The river crossing later gave the capital its name.

## Frank's Ford

The best-known story says the name came from a fight in 1780. A group of settlers from [Bryan's Station](/stories/bryan-station-siege-august-1782/) was on its way to make salt at [Mann's Lick](/stories/manns-lick-louisvilles-salt-town/) when Native warriors attacked them at the river. Pioneer Stephen Frank was killed, and settlers called the crossing "Frank's Ford." The name was later shortened to Frankfort.

One account links the name instead to settlers from [Frankfurt am Main](https://grokipedia.com/page/Frankfort,_Kentucky) in Germany. Another, the Frank's Ford story, is the one most historical records support.

## Wilkinson's town

In 1786 James Wilkinson bought land on the north side of the river, which became downtown Frankfort. That year the Virginia legislature set aside 100 acres as the town of Frankfort. Wilkinson promoted the town as a future capital. He believed farm produce could travel down the Kentucky River to the Ohio and Mississippi and on to New Orleans.

Daniel Gano and Daniel Weisiger helped lay out the settlement in 1787. Danger from attacks slowed settlement at first, and growth during the late 1780s was slow. Weisiger later became postmaster, and by 1794 Frankfort had a U.S. post office.

## Choosing a capital

Kentucky became the 15th state on June 1, 1792. On June 20 the legislature named five commissioners to pick a capital: John Allen and John Edwards of Bourbon County, Henry Lee of Mason, Thomas Kennedy of Madison and Robert Todd of Fayette. Several towns competed, including Lexington.

Frankfort won on December 5, 1792. Early histories credit the offer made through Andrew Holmes. It included his log house as a capitol for seven years, town lots, £50 worth of locks and hinges, 10 boxes of glass, 1,500 pounds of nails and $3,000 in gold. The town's central location and its place on the navigable Kentucky River also counted in its favor.

## A lasting capitol

In 1796 John Brown, one of Kentucky's first U.S. senators, built [Liberty Hall](/stories/liberty-hall-john-browns-frankfort-house/) in Frankfort. The legislature voted in 1827 to build a new capitol. Gideon Shryock, then only 25, designed the [Old State Capitol](https://grokipedia.com/page/old_state_capitol_%28kentucky%29) in the Greek Revival style. It was Kentucky's third capitol and housed the General Assembly from 1830 to 1910.

## Kentucky today

The Old State Capitol has been a museum and the home of the Kentucky Historical Society since 1920. It was named a National Historic Landmark in 1971. Frankfort is still Kentucky's capital, and in 2020 it had 28,602 people.
